entries.name: SendUserFile
entries.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

# Voice audition: renders the same two lines with Chatterbox (open-source, expressive TTS) at several
# expressiveness settings, so we can pick one by ear. Runs in GitHub Actions (CPU); output: samples/*.wav
import sys, time, traceback
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS

OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "samples"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

TEXT = ("Your competitor just doubled their ML team. And you? You'll find out next quarter! "
        "Or... you could ask Spend Radar. It reads your books, scans the market, "
        "and argues with itself before it tells you anything.")

# exaggeration: emotion intensity (0.5 = neutral). cfg_weight: lower = looser, more dramatic pacing.
SETTINGS = [("calm", 0.5, 0.5), ("lively", 0.75, 0.4), ("hype", 1.0, 0.3)]

model = ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device="cpu")
print("torch", torch.__version__, "sample rate", model.sr)
ok = 0
for name, exag, cfg in SETTINGS:
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        wav = model.generate(TEXT, exaggeration=exag, cfg_weight=cfg)
        ta.save(str(OUT / f"chatterbox_{name}_ex{exag}_cfg{cfg}.wav"), wav, model.sr)
        ok += 1
        print(f"{name}: {wav.shape[-1] / model.sr:.1f}s audio in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
    except Exception:
        traceback.print_exc()
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

# Renders the demo film in the cloud (the team laptops are too slow to render video).
# Runs only on pushes to the demo-video branch; main is untouched. Output: the "spend-radar-demo" artifact.
name: demo-video

on:
  push:
    branches: [demo-video]
    paths: ["demo-video/**", "site/**", ".github/workflows/demo-video.yml"]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: demo-video
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  prep:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    defaults: { run: { working-directory: demo-video } }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.12" }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: "20" }
      - name: System packages
        run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq espeak-ng ffmpeg fonts-dejavu-core
      - name: Python packages (CPU only)
        run: |
          pip install -q --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch
          pip install -q --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu kokoro soundfile scipy numpy
          python -c "import torch, transformers; from kokoro import KPipeline; print('torch', torch.__version__, 'transformers', transformers.__version__)"
      - name: Narration (Kokoro, local model)
        run: python tts.py
      - name: Music bed
        run: python music.py
      - name: Node packages
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund
      - name: Film the evidence site
        run: node record_site.mjs
      - name: Sound-effect cues and preview stills
        run: |
          node render.mjs --cues
          node render.mjs --stills auto
      - name: Mix audio
        run: python music.py --mix
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: prep
          path: demo-video/build
          retention-days: 3

  render:
    needs: prep
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix: { shard: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] }
    defaults: { run: { working-directory: demo-video } }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: "20" }
      - run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq ffmpeg fonts-dejavu-core
      - run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { name: prep, path: demo-video/build }
      - name: Render shard ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: node render.mjs --shard ${{ matrix.shard }} --shards 8
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: seg-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: demo-video/build/seg_${{ matrix.shard }}.mp4
          retention-days: 3

  assemble:
    needs: render
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq ffmpeg
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { name: prep, path: build }
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { pattern: seg-*, path: segs, merge-multiple: true }
      - name: Join, add audio, make a contact sheet
        run: |
          for i in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do echo "file 'segs/seg_$i.mp4'" >> list.txt; done
          ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -f concat -safe 0 -i list.txt -c copy video.mp4
          ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i video.mp4 -i build/audio.wav -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -shortest -movflags +faststart spend-radar-demo.mp4
          ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i spend-radar-demo.mp4 -vf "fps=1/5,scale=480:-1,tile=6x6" -frames:v 1 contact-sheet.png
          ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration:stream=codec_name,width,height -of compact spend-radar-demo.mp4 | tee probe.txt
          mkdir -p out && mv spend-radar-demo.mp4 contact-sheet.png probe.txt out/ && cp build/still_*.png build/timeline.json out/
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: spend-radar-demo
          path: out
          retention-days: 14

input.content:
# Voice audition: renders the same lines with Chatterbox (open-source, expressive TTS) so we can pick one by ear.
# Female versions clone the timbre of a short reference clip (a free Edge neural voice, made by refs.py);
# Chatterbox supplies the expressiveness. Runs in GitHub Actions (CPU); output: samples/*.wav
import sys, time, traceback
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
OUT = HERE / "samples"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

TEXT = ("Your competitor just doubled their ML team. And you? You'll find out next quarter! "
        "Or... you could ask Spend Radar. It reads your books, scans the market, "
        "and argues with itself before it tells you anything.")

# (name, reference clip or None for the built-in voice, exaggeration, cfg_weight)
# exaggeration: emotion intensity (0.5 = neutral). cfg_weight: lower = looser, more dramatic pacing.
SETTINGS = [
    ("female-ava_mix", HERE / "refs" / "ava.wav", 0.6, 0.45),
    ("female-emma_mix", HERE / "refs" / "emma.wav", 0.6, 0.45),
    ("female-jenny_mix", HERE / "refs" / "jenny.wav", 0.6, 0.45),
]

model = ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device="cpu")
print("torch", torch.__version__, "sample rate", model.sr)
ok = 0
for name, ref, exag, cfg in SETTINGS:
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        kw = {"audio_prompt_path": str(ref)} if ref else {}
        wav = model.generate(TEXT, exaggeration=exag, cfg_weight=cfg, **kw)
        ta.save(str(OUT / f"chatterbox_{name}_ex{exag}_cfg{cfg}.wav"), wav, model.sr)
        ok += 1
        print(f"{name}: {wav.shape[-1] / model.sr:.1f}s audio in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
    except Exception:
        traceback.print_exc()
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

# Female versions clone the timbre of a short reference clip (a free Edge neural voice, made by refs.py);
# Chatterbox supplies the expressiveness. Runs in GitHub Actions (CPU); output: samples/*.wav
import sys, time, traceback
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
OUT = HERE / "samples"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

TEXT = ("Your competitor just doubled their ML team. And you? You'll find out next quarter! "
        "Or... you could ask Spend Radar. It reads your books, scans the market, "
        "and argues with itself before it tells you anything.")

# (name, reference clip or None for the built-in voice, exaggeration, cfg_weight)
# exaggeration: emotion intensity (0.5 = neutral). cfg_weight: lower = looser, more dramatic pacing.
SETTINGS = [
    ("female-ava_mix", HERE / "refs" / "ava.wav", 0.6, 0.45),
    ("female-emma_mix", HERE / "refs" / "emma.wav", 0.6, 0.45),
    ("female-jenny_mix", HERE / "refs" / "jenny.wav", 0.6, 0.45),
]

model = ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device="cpu")
print("torch", torch.__version__, "sample rate", model.sr)
ok = 0
for name, ref, exag, cfg in SETTINGS:
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        kw = {"audio_prompt_path": str(ref)} if ref else {}
        wav = model.generate(TEXT, exaggeration=exag, cfg_weight=cfg, **kw)
        ta.save(str(OUT / f"chatterbox_{name}_ex{exag}_cfg{cfg}.wav"), wav, model.sr)
        ok += 1
        print(f"{name}: {wav.shape[-1] / model.sr:.1f}s audio in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
    except Exception:
        traceback.print_exc()
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

# Makes short female reference clips (free Edge neural voices) whose timbre Chatterbox clones: refs/<name>.wav
import asyncio, subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import edge_tts

REFS = Path(__file__).parent / "refs"
REFS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
TEXT = ("Oh, this is my favourite part! We tried something new this weekend, and honestly? "
        "It worked better than any of us expected. Let me show you how.")
VOICES = {"ava": "en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural", "emma": "en-US-EmmaMultilingualNeural", "jenny": "en-US-JennyNeural"}


async def main():
    for name, voice in VOICES.items():
        mp3 = REFS / f"{name}.mp3"
        await edge_tts.Communicate(TEXT, voice).save(str(mp3))
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", str(mp3), "-ar", "24000", "-ac", "1", str(REFS / f"{name}.wav")], check=True)
        print("ref", name)


asyncio.run(main())

content.thinking: I'll provide six new female voice options, each modeled on a real woman's voice from LibriSpeech (a CC BY 4.0 dataset verified at openslr.org/12), excluding Ava, Emma, and other Edge voices. Chatterbox will handle the speech synthesis at the calm-lively setting you specified.

input.content:
# Picks female reference voices from real human recordings (LibriSpeech dev-clean, CC BY 4.0, openslr.org/12)
# for Chatterbox to clone. Ranks the female readers by pitch variation (livelier readers first) and keeps the top N.
# Expects the extracted corpus at ./LibriSpeech. Writes refs/<speaker>.wav (24 kHz mono), refs/<speaker>.mp3, refs/chosen.json
import json, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

import librosa
import numpy as np
import soundfile as sf

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
CORPUS = HERE / "LibriSpeech"
REFS = HERE / "refs"
REFS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
KEEP = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6
TARGET_S = 12.0


def female_ids():
    """Speaker sex from SPEAKERS.TXT if the archive has it; else None (fall back to pitch)."""
    p = CORPUS / "SPEAKERS.TXT"
    if not p.exists():
        return None
    ids = set()
    for line in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").splitlines():
        if line.startswith(";"):
            continue
        parts = [x.strip() for x in line.split("|")]
        if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[1] == "F" and parts[2] == "dev-clean":
            ids.add(parts[0])
    return ids


def clip_for(spk_dir):
    """~12 s of consecutive utterances from the speaker's first chapter."""
    chapter = sorted(p for p in spk_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir())[0]
    audio, total = [], 0.0
    for f in sorted(chapter.glob("*.flac")):
        y, sr = sf.read(str(f))
        audio.append(y)
        audio.append(np.zeros(int(0.25 * sr)))
        total += len(y) / sr
        if total >= TARGET_S:
            break
    return np.concatenate(audio), sr


females = female_ids()
print("SPEAKERS.TXT female ids:", None if females is None else len(females))
rows = []
for spk_dir in sorted(p for p in (CORPUS / "dev-clean").iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
    spk = spk_dir.name
    if females is not None and spk not in females:
        continue
    y, sr = clip_for(spk_dir)
    y16 = librosa.resample(y, orig_sr=sr, target_sr=16000) if sr != 16000 else y
    f0, voiced, _ = librosa.pyin(y16, fmin=70, fmax=500, sr=16000)
    f0 = f0[voiced & ~np.isnan(f0)]
    if len(f0) < 50:
        continue
    median = float(np.median(f0))
    if females is None and median < 165:  # no sex labels: keep higher-pitched voices only
        continue
    spread = float(np.std(12 * np.log2(f0 / median)))  # pitch variation in semitones
    rows.append({"speaker": spk, "median_hz": round(median, 1), "pitch_spread_st": round(spread, 2), "seconds": round(len(y) / sr, 1)})
    rows[-1]["_audio"] = (y, sr)

rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r["pitch_spread_st"])
chosen = rows[:KEEP]
for r in chosen:
    y, sr = r.pop("_audio")
    wav = REFS / f"{r['speaker']}.wav"
    sf.write(str(wav), librosa.resample(y, orig_sr=sr, target_sr=24000), 24000)
    subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", str(wav), "-b:a", "128k", str(REFS / f"{r['speaker']}.mp3")], check=True)
for r in rows[KEEP:]:
    r.pop("_audio", None)
print(json.dumps(rows, indent=1))
(REFS / "chosen.json").write_text(json.dumps(chosen, indent=1))
print("chosen:", [r["speaker"] for r in chosen])

# Makes short female reference clips (free Edge neural voices) whose timbre Chatterbox clones: refs/<name>.wav
import asyncio, subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import edge_tts

REFS = Path(__file__).parent / "refs"
REFS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
TEXT = ("Oh, this is my favourite part! We tried something new this weekend, and honestly? "
        "It worked better than any of us expected. Let me show you how.")
VOICES = {"ava": "en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural", "emma": "en-US-EmmaMultilingualNeural", "jenny": "en-US-JennyNeural"}


async def main():
    for name, voice in VOICES.items():
        mp3 = REFS / f"{name}.mp3"
        await edge_tts.Communicate(TEXT, voice).save(str(mp3))
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", str(mp3), "-ar", "24000", "-ac", "1", str(REFS / f"{name}.wav")], check=True)
        print("ref", name)


asyncio.run(main())

import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS

OUT = HERE / "samples"

TEXT = ("Your competitor just doubled their ML team. And you? You'll find out next quarter! "
        "Or... you could ask Spend Radar. It reads your books, scans the market, "
        "and argues with itself before it tells you anything.")

# exaggeration: emotion intensity (0.5 = neutral). cfg_weight: lower = looser, more dramatic pacing.

    ("female-ava_mix", HERE / "refs" / "ava.wav", 0.6, 0.45),

]

        wav = model.generate(TEXT, exaggeration=exag, cfg_weight=cfg, **kw)
        ta.save(str(OUT / f"chatterbox_{name}_ex{exag}_cfg{cfg}.wav"), wav, model.sr)
        ok += 1
        print(f"{name}: {wav.shape[-1] / model.sr:.1f}s audio in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")

# 05 — Same data, three different audit verdicts

- **Symptom (what the traces showed):** the self-audit is meant to try to disprove each finding before it is reported. On identical Acme data, with the same model mix (gpt-5-nano + gemini-3.5-flash-lite, 0 fallback hops), the ML/AI finding got a different verdict depending on the run:

  | Run | Trace | ML/AI verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1010-767322 | `5c512d38b1cc95f99d0682619343c0b0` | confirmed |
  | 1010-bf52d4 | `d4a8716f6d2ed79322ca0d252764837e` | overturned |
  | 1010-4d1835 | `0dcf22977776591d6c8e47e0dffeed33` | downgraded |
  | 1010-bd4980 | `96bb795859c9f184fbcebb996b0e5b8f` | overturned |
  | 1010-a67b26 | `c4c0b55ade5fdbae4032698bc949e0ac` | overturned |

  Across all 23 finished Acme runs in `runs/`, the split was 3 confirmed / 12 downgraded / 8 overturned. Engineering, sales and marketing were stable (5/5 confirmed). The `audit:f_ml_ai` spans show the same input every time: a computed confidence of 0.00, plus "Honeycomb / Sentry ml_ai signals disagree" as the evidence against.

- **Root cause:** the deciding fact was already computed in Python. Two competitors' independent ML/AI signals contradict each other (agreement below 0.6). The verdict for that fact was nevertheless left to the LLM judge, which read the same evidence as "weakens it" in some runs and "proves it wrong" or "survives" in others. The brief's own split (§4.1) says Python decides what can be decided deterministically; this decision had slipped through to the LLM.

- **Fix:** branch `feat/deterministic-audit`, commit `bb2fb2f` (`spendradar/audit.py`).
  - A policy finding where any competitor's signals disagree (agreement < `AGREEMENT_MIN` = 0.6) is **downgraded deterministically**. Its confidence is halved, and the note names the competitors.
  - A policy finding with no evidence against it, after recomputation and source checks pass, is **confirmed deterministically**.
  - The LLM judge (and its second opinion) now only handles real judgement calls: news evidence, and mis-categorisation flags.
  - Unit test: `tests/test_report_audit.py::test_disagreeing_signals_downgrade_without_asking_the_llm`.

- **After:** `spendradar eval --n 5 --evidence --variant cs05-after-deterministic-audit`. Scorecard `evidence/evals/20261011T145242-bb2fb2f-cs05-after-deterministic-audit.json`, neatlogs eval trace `23dc44d364685f2d715d92bd8dce6194`.

  | Run | Trace | ML/AI verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1011-41090d | `bfd41c0e603782c9df549da8292fac15` | downgraded |
  | 1011-656492 | `2f61f9f5415d17b790ef4d97e6794101` | downgraded |
  | 1011-8ae79e | `c550b7b7b63566303e1ca322503d2a38` | downgraded |
  | 1011-e1f008 | `77a9f435452087e4a45f6ae9032ad340` | downgraded |
  | 1011-d1cade | `80803385d7b0ba70104eefb85a7574f7` | downgraded |

- **Numbers (n = 5 per side, same provider mix, 0 fallback hops on both sides):**

  | Metric | Before mean [min–max] | After mean [min–max] |
  |---|---|---|
  | **Distinct ML/AI verdicts across 5 identical runs** | **3** | **1** |
  | **Runs agreeing with the most common verdict** | **3/5** | **5/5** |
  | Planted errors caught | 5/5 [5–5] | 5/5 [5–5] |
  | Unsupported numbers in report | 0 | 0 |
  | False alarms | 0 | 0 |
  | Other policy findings stable (eng / sales / marketing) | 5/5 each | 5/5 each |
  | LLM calls per run | 29.8 [29–30] | 25.8 [25–26] |
  | Output tokens per run | 66,327 [62,274–68,930] | 57,184 [54,509–60,307] |
  | LLM latency per run (s) | 329.7 [310.9–360.5] | 281.3 [264.2–288.5] |

- **Caveats, stated plainly:**
  - The before batch ran at commits `bb61e37`/`e896b86`. Other changes (held-out-company fixes, the line-item check, hardening) also landed between the two sides. The verdict stability is attributable to this fix, because every after-run's `audit:f_ml_ai` note reads "deterministic: competitor signals disagree…". The drop in LLM calls, tokens and latency is **indicative only**: part of it comes from skipping the judge on the other policy findings, and part may come from the other commits.
  - "Downgraded" is a policy choice: a gap built on contradicting signals may be real, but it is not confirmed. It matches the majority verdict before the fix (12 of 23 runs). It also satisfies the planted fixture (Sentry Marketing ×5), which expects a downgrade or overturn: fixture run `1011-2b916a` (trace `61f10e4d251c44b8674ac263b353efa2`, scorecard `evidence/evals/20261011T145816-bb2fb2f-dirty-cs05-after-fixture.json`) caught **6/6**, with the marketing finding downgraded deterministically (confidence 0.041) and 0 fallback hops. The `-dirty` tag on that scorecard is only this file and the new unit test, which were uncommitted when it ran.
  - This removes variance, not judgement. The LLM still decides cases that need reading (news, mis-categorisation).

- **Review by Entire trail runners (trail #2):** the review runner raised a medium finding (`01M4N4SF2YQX`). When signals disagree **and** there is negative news, the shortcut skipped the judge, so the news was never weighed. Fixed in the next commit: the shortcut now applies only when there is no news evidence. With news, the judge decides, floored at "downgrade" (it can overturn on the news, never confirm). Regression test: `test_disagreeing_signals_with_news_still_go_to_the_judge`. I recomputed the evidence for all 6 after-runs above (5 real + 1 fixture): none had news on a disagreeing finding, so the measured results are unchanged.

# Narration, one line at a time, with Chatterbox cloning the chosen reader (refs/<speaker>.wav).
# Each take is checked with Whisper: if the words heard don't match the script, it retries with a new seed
# and keeps the best take. Runs as one of N parallel shards in GitHub Actions (CPU).
#   python tts_lines.py <shard> <shards>  ->  ../build/voice/lines/<line id>.wav + .json (score, seed, word times)
import difflib, json, re, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS
from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
from num2words import num2words

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
OUT = ROOT / "build" / "voice" / "lines"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
SEEDS = (11, 23, 37, 51)
GOOD = 0.9  # accept a take once its words match the script this closely

shard, shards = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
script = json.loads((ROOT / "script.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
voice = script["voice"]
speaker = voice["reference"].split("reader ")[1].split()[0]
ref = HERE / "refs" / f"{speaker}.wav"
lines = [l for s in script["scenes"] for l in s["lines"]]

# Longest-first greedy split so shards finish at about the same time.
loads, mine = [0] * shards, []
for i, l in sorted(enumerate(lines), key=lambda x: -len(x[1]["say"])):
    k = loads.index(min(loads))
    loads[k] += len(l["say"])
    if k == shard:
        mine.append(l)


def norm(text):
    t = text.lower().replace("$", "")
    t = re.sub(r"(?<=\d),(?=\d)", "", t)
    t = re.sub(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?", lambda m: " " + num2words(float(m.group()) if "." in m.group() else int(m.group())) + " ", t)
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", t)


model = ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device="cpu")
asr = WhisperModel("base.en", device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
print(f"shard {shard}/{shards}: {[l['id'] for l in mine]}")

for l in mine:
    best = None
    for seed in SEEDS:
        t0 = time.time()
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        wav = model.generate(l["say"], audio_prompt_path=str(ref),
                             exaggeration=l.get("exag", voice["exaggeration"]), cfg_weight=voice["cfg_weight"])
        tmp = OUT / f"{l['id']}.take.wav"
        ta.save(str(tmp), wav, model.sr)
        segs, _ = asr.transcribe(str(tmp), language="en", beam_size=5, word_timestamps=True)
        words = [{"w": w.word.strip(), "start": round(w.start, 3), "end": round(w.end, 3)} for s in segs for w in s.words]
        heard = " ".join(w["w"] for w in words)
        score = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, norm(l["say"]), norm(heard)).ratio()
        print(f"  {l['id']} seed {seed}: score {score:.3f} in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s | heard: {heard}")
        if best is None or score > best["score"]:
            best = {"id": l["id"], "seed": seed, "score": round(score, 3), "heard": heard, "words": words, "sr": model.sr}
            tmp.replace(OUT / f"{l['id']}.wav")
        else:
            tmp.unlink()
        if score >= GOOD:
            break
    (OUT / f"{l['id']}.json").write_text(json.dumps(best, indent=1))
    if best["score"] < GOOD:
        print(f"  WARNING {l['id']}: best take only {best['score']:.3f}")

# Joins the narration lines into one track and writes the timeline every other step follows.
#   ../build/voice/lines/*.wav + .json  ->  ../build/voice.wav (48 kHz mono) + ../build/timeline.json
# Each take is trimmed to its first/last spoken word (Whisper times), so no stray breaths or tails.
# timeline.json: fps, duration, scenes[{id,start,end}], lines[{id,scene,start,dur,cap,say,words[{w,t0,t1}]}],
#                env (voice loudness per video frame, 0..1, for anything that should move with the voice)
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import soundfile as sf
from scipy.signal import resample_poly

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
LINES = ROOT / "build" / "voice" / "lines"
FPS, SR = 30, 48000
GAP = 0.16  # between lines in the same scene

script = json.loads((ROOT / "script.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
t = 0.0
track, scenes, out_lines = [], [], []


def place(samples, at):
    end = int(at * SR) + len(samples)
    if sum(len(x) for x in track) < end:
        track.append(np.zeros(end - sum(len(x) for x in track)))
    buf = np.concatenate(track)
    buf[int(at * SR):end] += samples
    track[:] = [buf]


for sc in script["scenes"]:
    t += sc.get("pad_before", 0.2)
    s0 = t
    for i, l in enumerate(sc["lines"]):
        meta = json.loads((LINES / f"{l['id']}.json").read_text())
        y, sr = sf.read(str(LINES / f"{l['id']}.wav"))
        words = meta["words"]
        a = max(0.0, words[0]["start"] - 0.06) if words else 0.0
        b = min(len(y) / sr, words[-1]["end"] + 0.14) if words else len(y) / sr
        y = y[int(a * sr):int(b * sr)]
        fade = int(0.012 * sr)
        y[:fade] *= np.linspace(0, 1, fade)
        y[-fade:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, fade)
        y48 = resample_poly(y, SR, sr)
        start = round(t * FPS) / FPS
        place(y48, start)
        dur = len(y48) / SR
        out_lines.append({
            "id": l["id"], "scene": sc["id"], "start": round(start, 3), "dur": round(dur, 3),
            "cap": l["cap"], "say": l["say"], "score": meta["score"],
            "words": [{"w": w["w"], "t0": round(start + w["start"] - a, 3), "t1": round(start + w["end"] - a, 3)} for w in words],
        })
        t = start + dur + (GAP if i < len(sc["lines"]) - 1 else 0)
    t += sc.get("pad_after", 0.25)
    scenes.append({"id": sc["id"], "start": round(s0 - sc.get("pad_before", 0.2), 3), "end": round(t, 3)})

dur = round(t * FPS) / FPS
voice = np.concatenate(track) if track else np.zeros(1)
voice = np.pad(voice, (0, max(0, int(dur * SR) - len(voice))))[: int(dur * SR)]
peak = np.max(np.abs(voice)) or 1.0
voice = voice / peak * 0.89
sf.write(str(ROOT / "build" / "voice.wav"), voice.astype(np.float32), SR)

# Loudness per video frame: RMS over the frame, fast attack / slower release, gated, 0..1.
hop = SR // FPS
rms = np.array([np.sqrt(np.mean(voice[i:i + hop] ** 2)) for i in range(0, len(voice), hop)])
rms = rms / (np.percentile(rms, 98) or 1)
env, v = [], 0.0
for r in rms:
    v = r if r > v else v * 0.72 + r * 0.28
    env.append(round(float(min(1.0, max(0.0, (v - 0.06) / 0.94))), 3))

tl = {"fps": FPS, "duration": dur, "scenes": scenes, "lines": out_lines, "env": env}
(ROOT / "build" / "timeline.json").write_text(json.dumps(tl))
print(f"duration {dur:.2f}s, {len(out_lines)} lines")
for l in out_lines:
    print(f"  {l['start']:7.2f} +{l['dur']:5.2f}  {l['id']:7s} score {l['score']:.3f}  {l['cap']}")

        y[-fade:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, fade)

        start = round(t * FPS) / FPS
        place(y48, start)
        dur = len(y48) / SR
        out_lines.append({
            "id": l["id"], "scene": sc["id"], "start": round(start, 3), "dur": round(dur, 3),
            "cap": l["cap"], "say": l["say"], "score": meta["score"],
            "words": [{"w": w["w"], "t0": round(start + w["start"] - a, 3), "t1": round(start + w["end"] - a, 3)} for w in words],

rms = rms / (np.percentile(rms, 98) or 1)

    v = r if r > v else v * 0.72 + r * 0.28
    env.append(round(float(min(1.0, max(0.0, (v - 0.06) / 0.94))), 3))

tl = {"fps": FPS, "duration": dur, "scenes": scenes, "lines": out_lines, "env": env}
(ROOT / "build" / "timeline.json").write_text(json.dumps(tl))
print(f"duration {dur:.2f}s, {len(out_lines)} lines")
for l in out_lines:
    print(f"  {l['start']:7.2f} +{l['dur']:5.2f}  {l['id']:7s} score {l['score']:.3f}  {l['cap']}")

# Demo film v2, rendered in the cloud (team laptops are too slow for video).
# narration (Chatterbox, cached per script) -> site capture -> timeline + music -> Remotion render in shards -> MP4.
# Runs only on the demo-video branch. Output: the "spend-radar-film" artifact.
name: demo-film

on:
  push:
    branches: [demo-video]
    paths: ["demo-video/**", "!demo-video/comp/**", "site/**", ".github/workflows/demo-film.yml"]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: demo-film
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  SHARDS: 8

jobs:
  # ── narration: one job per slice of lines, skipped when the cache already has this script's voice ──
  voice-key:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.k.outputs.key }}
      hit: ${{ steps.c.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: k
        run: echo "key=voice-v2-${{ hashFiles('demo-video/script.json', 'demo-video/voice/tts_lines.py', 'demo-video/voice/refs.py') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - id: c
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with: { path: demo-video/build/voice/lines, key: "${{ steps.k.outputs.key }}", lookup-only: true }

  voice:
    needs: voice-key
    if: needs.voice-key.outputs.hit != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 50
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix: { shard: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] }
    defaults: { run: { working-directory: demo-video/voice } }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.11" }
      - run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq ffmpeg
      - name: Python packages (CPU torch)
        run: pip install -q --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu chatterbox-tts faster-whisper num2words librosa soundfile
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with: { path: demo-video/voice/dev-clean.tar.gz, key: librispeech-dev-clean }
      - name: Reference reader (LibriSpeech dev-clean, CC BY 4.0)
        run: |
          [ -f dev-clean.tar.gz ] || curl -sSfL https://openslr.elda.org/resources/12/dev-clean.tar.gz -o dev-clean.tar.gz || curl -sSfL https://openslr.trmal.net/resources/12/dev-clean.tar.gz -o dev-clean.tar.gz
          tar xzf dev-clean.tar.gz
          python refs.py --speaker "$(python -c "import json;print(json.load(open('../script.json'))['voice']['reference'].split('reader ')[1].split()[0])")"
      - name: Lines (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        run: python tts_lines.py ${{ matrix.shard }} 6
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with: { name: "voice-${{ matrix.shard }}", path: demo-video/build/voice/lines, retention-days: 3 }

  voice-save:
    needs: [voice-key, voice]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4

# Local stand-in for build/timeline.json (the real one comes from the narration in CI): estimates each line's
# length and word times from the script at ~2.9 words/s, so stills can be checked before the voice exists.
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
script = json.loads((ROOT / "script.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
FPS, WPS = 30, 2.9
t, scenes, lines = 0.0, [], []
for sc in script["scenes"]:
    s0 = t
    t += sc.get("pad_before", 0.2)
    for i, l in enumerate(sc["lines"]):
        words = l["say"].split()
        start, words_out = round(t * FPS) / FPS, []
        for w in words:
            d = 0.12 + 0.045 * len(w)
            words_out.append({"w": w, "t0": round(t, 3), "t1": round(t + d, 3)})
            t += d + (0.25 if w[-1] in ".,!?" else 0.03)
        lines.append({"id": l["id"], "scene": sc["id"], "start": start, "dur": round(t - start, 3), "cap": l["cap"], "say": l["say"], "score": 1, "words": words_out})
        t += 0.16 if i < len(sc["lines"]) - 1 else 0
    t += sc.get("pad_after", 0.25)
    scenes.append({"id": sc["id"], "start": round(s0, 3), "end": round(t, 3)})
dur = round(t * FPS) / FPS
env = [0.0] * int(dur * FPS)
for l in lines:
    for w in l["words"]:
        for f in range(int(w["t0"] * FPS), int(w["t1"] * FPS)):
            env[f] = 0.75
(ROOT / "build").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(ROOT / "build" / "timeline.json").write_text(json.dumps({"fps": FPS, "duration": dur, "scenes": scenes, "lines": lines, "env": env, "dev": True}))
print(f"dev timeline: {dur:.1f}s, {len(lines)} lines")

lines: +# Publishes the static evidence site (site/) to GitHub Pages on every push to main.
+# The site is plain HTML/CSS/JS reading site/data.js; nothing is built and no secrets are used.
- `entire graph search` / `impact` were used to locate and size changes, e.g. the callers of `decide_recovery` before changing the recovery menu.

- **`spendradar explain <trace_id | run_id>`: from a neatlogs span to the agent session that wrote the code.** For each failing span (or `--span decide:recovery`) it writes a dossier. Each dossier holds the span's input, output and error; the exact code line (refined to the line that raises that error); `entire why` (commit, Entire checkpoint, coding-agent session, model, and the prompt that produced the line, secret-scrubbed); and `entire graph impact` (callers that a fix would affect). Auto-instrumented LLM spans resolve through their parent span. On the corrupt-PDF bug the chain closes: neatlogs auto-triage flagged the Gemini 400 → `read_pdf` → the guard at `files.py:139` → checkpoint `01M4K4TJ…`, whose prompt *is* the neatlogs triage task. # Narration, one line at a time, with Chatterbox cloning the chosen reader (refs/<speaker>.wav).
# Each take is checked with Whisper: if the words heard don't match the script, it retries with a new seed
# and keeps the best take. Runs as one of N parallel shards in GitHub Actions (CPU).
#   python tts_lines.py <shard> <shards>  ->  ../build/voice/lines/<line id>.wav + .json (score, seed, word times)
import difflib, json, re, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torchaudio as ta
from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS
from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
from num2words import num2words

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
OUT = ROOT / "build" / "voice" / "lines"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
SEEDS = (11, 23, 37, 51)
GOOD = 0.9  # accept a take once its words match the script this closely

shard, shards = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
script = json.loads((ROOT / "script.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
voice = script["voice"]
speaker = voice["reference"].split("reader ")[1].split()[0]
ref = HERE / "refs" / f"{speaker}.wav"
lines = [l for s in script["scenes"] for l in s["lines"]]

# Longest-first greedy split so shards finish at about the same time.
loads, mine = [0] * shards, []
for i, l in sorted(enumerate(lines), key=lambda x: -len(x[1]["say"])):
    k = loads.index(min(loads))
    loads[k] += len(l["say"])
    if k == shard:
        mine.append(l)


def norm(text):
    t = text.lower().replace("$", "").replace("%", " percent")
    t = re.sub(r"(?<=\d),(?=\d)", "", t)
    t = re.sub(r"(?<=\d)\s+\.(?=\d)", ".", t)  # Whisper writes "26 .6"
    t = re.sub(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?", lambda m: " " + num2words(float(m.group()) if "." in m.group() else int(m.group())) + " ", t)
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", t)


model = ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device="cpu")
asr = WhisperModel("small.en", device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
print(f"shard {shard}/{shards}: {[l['id'] for l in mine]}")

for l in mine:
    exag = l.get("exag", voice["exaggeration"])
    old = OUT / f"{l['id']}.json"
    if old.exists() and (OUT / f"{l['id']}.wav").exists():  # reuse a cached take if it is for this exact line
        prev = json.loads(old.read_text())
        same = prev.get("say", l["say"]) == l["say"] and prev.get("exag", exag) == exag
        if same and difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, norm(l["say"]), norm(prev["heard"])).ratio() >= 0.85:
            print(f"  {l['id']}: cached take (seed {prev['seed']})")
            continue
    best = None
    for seed in SEEDS:
        t0 = time.time()
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        wav = model.generate(l["say"], audio_prompt_path=str(ref),
                             exaggeration=exag, cfg_weight=voice["cfg_weight"])
        tmp = OUT / f"{l['id']}.take.wav"
        ta.save(str(tmp), wav, model.sr)
        segs, _ = asr.transcribe(str(tmp), language="en", beam_size=5, word_timestamps=True)
        words = [{"w": w.word.strip(), "start": round(w.start, 3), "end": round(w.end, 3)} for s in segs for w in s.words]
        heard = " ".join(w["w"] for w in words)
        score = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, norm(l["say"]), norm(heard)).ratio()
        print(f"  {l['id']} seed {seed}: score {score:.3f} in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s | heard: {heard}")
        if best is None or score > best["score"]:
            best = {"id": l["id"], "say": l["say"], "exag": exag, "seed": seed, "score": round(score, 3), "heard": heard, "words": words, "sr": model.sr}
            tmp.replace(OUT / f"{l['id']}.wav")
        else:
            tmp.unlink()
        if score >= GOOD:
            break
    (OUT / f"{l['id']}.json").write_text(json.dumps(best, indent=1))
    if best["score"] < GOOD:
        print(f"  WARNING {l['id']}: best take only {best['score']:.3f}")

# Demo film v2, rendered in the cloud (team laptops are too slow for video).
# narration (Chatterbox, cached per script) -> site capture -> timeline + music -> Remotion render in shards -> MP4.
# Runs only on the demo-video branch. Output: the "spend-radar-film" artifact.
name: demo-film

on:
  push:
    branches: [demo-video]
    paths: ["demo-video/**", "!demo-video/comp/**", "site/**", ".github/workflows/demo-film.yml"]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: demo-film
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  SHARDS: 8

jobs:
  # ── narration: one job per slice of lines, skipped when the cache already has this script's voice ──
  voice-key:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.k.outputs.key }}
      hit: ${{ steps.c.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: k
        run: echo "key=voice-v2-${{ hashFiles('demo-video/script.json', 'demo-video/voice/tts_lines.py', 'demo-video/voice/refs.py') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - id: c
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with: { path: demo-video/build/voice/lines, key: "${{ steps.k.outputs.key }}", lookup-only: true }

  voice:
    needs: voice-key
    if: needs.voice-key.outputs.hit != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 50
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix: { shard: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] }
    defaults: { run: { working-directory: demo-video/voice } }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.11" }
      - run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq ffmpeg
      - name: Python packages (CPU torch)
        run: pip install -q --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu chatterbox-tts faster-whisper num2words librosa soundfile
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with: { path: demo-video/voice/dev-clean.tar.gz, key: librispeech-dev-clean }
      - name: Reference reader (LibriSpeech dev-clean, CC BY 4.0)
        run: |
          [ -f dev-clean.tar.gz ] || curl -sSfL https://openslr.elda.org/resources/12/dev-clean.tar.gz -o dev-clean.tar.gz || curl -sSfL https://openslr.trmal.net/resources/12/dev-clean.tar.gz -o dev-clean.tar.gz
          tar xzf dev-clean.tar.gz
          python refs.py --speaker "$(python -c "import json;print(json.load(open('../script.json'))['voice']['reference'].split('reader ')[1].split()[0])")"
      - name: Lines (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        run: python tts_lines.py ${{ matrix.shard }} 6
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with: { name: "voice-${{ matrix.shard }}", path: demo-video/build/voice/lines, retention-days: 3 }

  voice-save:
    needs: [voice-key, voice]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { pattern: voice-*, path: demo-video/build/voice/lines, merge-multiple: true }
      - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with: { path: demo-video/build/voice/lines, key: "${{ needs.voice-key.outputs.key }}" }

  # ── timeline, music and mix ──
  prep:
    needs: [voice-key, voice-save]
    if: always() && needs.voice-key.result == 'success' && (needs.voice-save.result == 'success' || needs.voice-key.outputs.hit == 'true')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    defaults: { run: { working-directory: demo-video } }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.11" }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: "20" }
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with: { path: demo-video/build/voice/lines, key: "${{ needs.voice-key.outputs.key }}", fail-on-cache-miss: true }
      - run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq ffmpeg && pip install -q numpy scipy soundfile
      - name: Timeline + voice track
        run: python voice/align.py
      - name: Music bed, sound-effect cues, mix
        run: |
          python music.py
          node film/cues.mjs
          python music.py --mix
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: prep
          path: |
            demo-video/build/timeline.json
            demo-video/build/audio.wav
            demo-video/build/voice.wav
            demo-video/build/cues.json
          retention-days: 3

# Builds film/src/data/*.json from the project's own evidence, so every number on screen traces to a file:
#   run.json   the featured run, from runs/1011-777bb7/state.json + report.md (runs/ is git-ignored, so the
#              derived file is committed and names its source)
#   facts.json summary counts, cfo.ai cash curves, Entire/explain details
# Run from the repo root:  python demo-video/film/make_data.py
import json, re
from pathlib import Path

import openpyxl

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "src" / "data"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
RUN = "1011-777bb7"

# ── the featured run ──
s = json.loads((ROOT / "runs" / RUN / "state.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
short = lambda x, n=90: (x if len(x) <= n else x[: n - 1] + "…")


def target(t):
    a = t.get("args") or {}
    return a.get("path") or a.get("name") or a.get("domain") or ""


tasks = [{"id": t["id"], "tool": t["tool"], "target": target(t), "status": t["status"], "recovery": (t.get("reason") or "").startswith("recovery:") or bool(t.get("parent"))} for t in s["done"]]
decisions = [{"task": d["task_id"], "check": short(d["failed_check"], 120), "options": d["options"], "chosen": d["chosen"], "default": d["default"],
              "overrode": d["chosen"] != d["default"], "reason": short(d["reason"], 140), "model": d["model"]} for d in s["decisions"]]
checks = s["checks"]
findings = [{"id": f["id"], "category": f["category"], "status": f.get("status"), "confidence": f.get("confidence"),

**VO:** "We also broke it on purpose: forced rate limits from Crustdata and the LLM. Three runs, every planted error still caught. When a check fails, the model picks a recovery from a fixed menu. In a hundred and sixty-one of two hundred and eighty-nine decisions it chose something other than the default rule."
[summary: injected_runs 3, all planted caught; recovery_overrides 161, recovery_decisions 289]

## 2:10–2:35 · cfo.ai
**On screen:** site **cfo.ai business plan** page (callout, then the tiers table). Cut to the cfo.ai Summary page.
**VO:** "Cfo dot A I built the business plan from measured costs. The model costs under three cents a run. Competitor data costs six to nine dollars, about ninety-nine percent of the cost. So caching decides the margin: capping fresh data at ten runs a month lifts the Team tier to seventy-six point six percent. Base case: cash-flow positive in month fifteen."
[business/cfoai_plan.md: $0.0285 per run, $6.24–$9.24, ~99%, 76.6%, Jan 2028 (month 15)]

## 2:35–2:50 · Close
**On screen:** **neatlogs** page (detections, evals, the auto-triage fix) scrolling, then the repo on GitHub.
**VO:** "Sixty-one scored runs, each with its trace, its commit and its checkpoint. Spend Radar, by team qwep. Hashtag neatHack."
[summary: runs_scored 61]

---

Spoken word count: 410, roughly 2.7 min at 150 words a minute. If it runs long, cut the latency sentence in 0:55–1:30 first, then the code-graph sentence in Entire.

**Do not say:** "AI-powered", "magic", any number not in brackets above. If a number changes after a new export, update it here from `evidence/frontend_data.json` before recording.
